result.summary: Adds a single new vector to tx_valid.json that exercises the positive direction of the FindAndDelete behavior implicated in CVE-2024-38365, where btcd's overly aggressive matching caused a chain split with Bitcoin Core. The vector uses a P2SH redeemScript with a signature embedded in a larger, non-matching push so that FindAndDelete finds nothing to delete and the transaction validates under Core's rules but would fail under btcd's old behavior. Author confirmed the vector discriminates correctly by patching EvalChecksigPreTapscript to mimic btcd's deletion and observing the test fail.
result.problem: The historical CVE-2024-38365 chain split stemmed from FindAndDelete only matching whole pushes at opcode boundaries; existing test vectors (script_FindAndDelete, tx_invalid.json) covered the failure side of this rule but not the positive case where a transaction must be accepted because nothing is deleted, leaving a coverage gap that test maintainers and future implementers of consensus-critical code would care about.
